subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Borges and the Mind-Bending Tale
description: A 60-second lesson on Borges and the Mind-Bending Tale.

hook.text: Jorge Luis Borges wrote stories about infinite libraries, forking timelines, and maps as large as the territory.

buildup.text: The Library of Babel describes a universe made entirely of books containing every possible combination of letters.

discovery.text: Borges disguised philosophy as fiction, turning metaphysical problems into compelling narrative puzzles.

twist.text: He went completely blind by his fifties and had to dictate his later stories entirely from memory.

climax.text: Borges proved that a short story can contain an entire universe if the idea at its center is powerful enough.

punchline.text: A blind man imagined infinite libraries in his mind.

quiz.question: What challenge did Borges face while writing his later stories?
options: He went completely blind and had to dictate from memory
He lost the ability to speak
